roadmap.item: R1 [HIGH PRIORITY] — Pull a workbook from Tableau Server/Cloud by link
roadmap.detail: INGEST HALF LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-28, same session it was built. Vendored tableau_server.py (sign_in_with_pat, find_workbook_by_content_url, download_workbook_bytes, fetch_workbook) — trimmed from the tableau skill's rest_api_client.py, kept fully inside the repo so the SiS deploy bundle has no external dependency. parse_tableau_url() handles both Cloud and self-hosted Server URL shapes, raises (never guesses) on an unrecognized one. pipeline_app.py's Discover & Scope tab gained a 'Source' radio — 'Pull from Tableau Server/Cloud' downloads via a URL + Fetch button and hands the bytes to the SAME run_pipeline()/pipeline.onboard() path as a manual upload (a tiny _FetchedWorkbook shim supplies .name/.getvalue()) — zero pipeline changes needed. PAT via TABLEAU_PAT_NAME/TABLEAU_PAT_SECRET only, never entered in the UI. Offline gate test_tableau_server_url_parsing_and_fetch (URL parsing + full request-shaping via a monkeypatched requests module). requests added to environment.yml; tableau_server.py added to snowflake.yml's pipeline_demo artifacts (caught mechanically by test_pipeline_demo_bundle_complete). LIVE-VERIFIED against the real account (site b360bi on prod-useast-b.online.tableau.com): PAT sign-in succeeded; find_workbook_by_content_url correctly resolved 5 different pasted-URL slugs to their real Tableau workbook ids. Downloading pre-existing site content hit a real, consistent 403019 across 4 different workbooks — a site-wide/role-wide 'Download workbook' permission gap on the account used for testing, not a bug in our request shaping (confirmed by the API getting far enough to name the specific workbook it refused). Published a copy of Superstore.twbx to the site (REST multipart publish, ad hoc — publish is out of R1's read scope, not added to tableau_server.py) to get download-authorized content, then pulled it straight back down through the ACTUAL fetch_workbook() function using a realistic view URL: valid .twbx bytes, correct internal structure (4 data files + Superstore.twb). Fed those bytes into pipeline.onboard() unchanged — 4 datasources resolved, zero missing, zero blocked. Ran the full CLI pipeline (convert.py) end to end on the downloaded bytes: 21 sheets, 0 blockers; queried the resulting app's grand totals and CustomerOverview figures — EXACT match to validate_numbers.py's Tableau-verified ground truth (Sales 2,326,534.35 vs 2,326,534; Profit 292,296.81 vs 292,297; Quantity 38,654 vs 38,654; Profit Ratio 0.1256 vs 0.126). Test artifacts (temp .twbx, generated IR/app) deleted after; reports/migration_assessment.md + sql/generated_views.sql (NOT stem-namespaced — a real shared-fixed-path characteristic of report.py, worth knowing, not a bug introduced here) got overwritten by the test run and were regenerated from the real Superstore.twbx to restore them; full regression suite re-confirmed all green after. The published test workbook was left on the site at the user's choice, not deleted. STILL OPEN: (a) a real client workbook download will need actual 'Download workbook' permission granted by a Tableau admin — this session's account didn't have it for pre-existing content; (b) the download_view_image/view-data pull that feeds R2's tableau_truth (per-section RENDERED values, not just workbook download) — untouched this pass, the other half of R1's original scope. SAME-SESSION FOLLOW-UP: deployed the app and tried the URL flow live in Snowsight — the honest missing-PAT error fired again, correctly, but for a reason the first pass hadn't handled: a Streamlit-in-Snowflake app has NO OS-env-var mechanism at all (TABLEAU_PAT_NAME/SECRET only work for local dev) and ZERO outbound internet access by default (reaching Tableau needs an External Access Integration). Fixed in code: new tableau_server._pat_from_sis_secret() reads a Snowflake SECRET object via _snowflake.get_username_password() (only importable inside SiS; returns (None, None) outside it, never raises); fetch_workbook's resolution order is now explicit args -> env vars -> SiS-bound secret; the error message names both the secret AND network-egress gaps explicitly. New tableau_server_sis_setup.sql (network rule + PASSWORD-type secret named 'tableau_pat' + external access integration + ALTER STREAMLIT binding) for the user to fill in their real PAT and run themselves in Snowsight — the assistant does not run this with the literal token, same credential rule as everywhere else in this project. Gate extended (same test, not a new one) with a mocked _snowflake module proving both the outside-SiS no-op and the inside-SiS resolution + actual use in the signin call. Pyflakes clean. Redeployed pipeline_demo a second time with the fix (user re-confirmed before each deploy push). The account-side SQL setup itself has NOT been run yet — R1's code is ready, but the deployed app will keep showing 'no PAT configured' until tableau_server_sis_setup.sql is executed against wb19670-c2gpartners. DIAGNOSED WHY THE FIRST SETUP ATTEMPT LEFT NOTHING BEHIND: user reported having already run tableau_server_sis_setup.sql, but DESCRIBE STREAMLIT + SHOW NETWORK RULES/SECRETS/EXTERNAL ACCESS INTEGRATIONS (all read-only, no account changes) confirmed zero objects exist — the script failed at its very first privileged statement. Root cause: this project's own `wbr` connection role is WBR_OWNER (SELECT CURRENT_ROLE() confirmed), a schema-scoped role lacking CREATE SECRET / CREATE NETWORK RULE / CREATE EXTERNAL ACCESS INTEGRATION (the last is account-level, not schema-scoped at all); user confirmed no ACCOUNTADMIN access. User asked to hardcode the PAT into the code instead as a workaround — declined, explained plainly rather than just citing policy: (a) a literal token in a file pushed to a live Snowflake stage (and exposed to git history) is treated like any other credential; (b) it would not even fix the problem, since SiS's zero-egress network sandboxing is independent of where the credential is stored — a hardcoded PAT would still hit the same blocked outbound call. Offered running locally instead (zero admin dependency, live-proven earlier this session) — user correctly pointed out that doesn't produce a Snowsight-hosted demo others can click into, which is true and was said plainly, not glossed over. Delivered the narrow-privilege path the user asked for: new tableau_server_sis_grants_request.sql — exactly 3 GRANT statements (CREATE INTEGRATION ON ACCOUNT, CREATE NETWORK RULE ON SCHEMA WBR_DB.PUBLIC, CREATE SECRET ON SCHEMA WBR_DB.PUBLIC, all TO ROLE WBR_OWNER — not ACCOUNTADMIN itself; WBR_OWNER already owns pipeline_demo so no extra grant needed for the final ALTER STREAMLIT). tableau_server_sis_setup.sql updated to comment out its USE ROLE ACCOUNTADMIN line and point at the grants file, so WBR_OWNER can run the whole setup directly once those 3 grants land. CURRENT STATE: waiting on the user to get those grants from their account admin; nothing else blocking. CLOSED OUT SAME SESSION: admin granted the 3 privileges; user ran tableau_server_sis_setup.sql themselves as WBR_OWNER; DESCRIBE STREAMLIT (checked independently by the assistant, read-only) confirmed external_access_integrations=['TABLEAU_ACCESS_INTEGRATION'] and external_access_secrets={'tableau_pat': 'WBR_DB.PUBLIC.TABLEAU_PAT_SECRET'} both bound correctly. Fixed parse_tableau_url to detect an all-digit /workbooks/<id> segment and raise a clear, specific error (open a view or use Share -> Copy Link) instead of silently attempting a doomed contentUrl lookup. User then asked for a project/workbook DROPDOWN instead of pasting links at all -- correctly identified this sidesteps URL-shape guessing entirely, not just today's bug. Built: parse_site_url (lenient, works from any pasted site link), TableauRestClient.list_projects/list_workbooks with a new paginated GET helper (caught for real that the site has 136 workbooks, not the 100 an unpaginated call had shown), list_site_contents (self-contained sign-in/list/sign-out), fetch_workbook_by_id (downloads by a known real id, no URL parsing at all), and _resolve_pat extracted as a shared helper. pipeline_app.py's Tableau panel restructured to Connect -> Project selectbox -> Workbook selectbox -> Fetch, with the old link-paste mode kept as a collapsed fallback expander (not removed). Gated (same test extended again): parse_site_url, pagination proven against a mocked 2-page response, fetch_workbook_by_id's request shaping, the numeric-id rejection. Restricted by a real correctness guard, _is_pure_sum_sql(m['sql']) -- only a bare SUM(col) expression may be approximated; a compound formula (ratio, LOD) is NEVER summed across rows, since summing per-row ratios is not the grand-total ratio (this guard is gated directly: a Profit Ratio-style compound metric is proven to never appear in the approximate output even when its caption matches a CSV column). RAW-COLUMN GROUND TRUTH WIRED 2026-07-30 -- a real gap the whole R1/R2 arc walked past, found when the user asked why Discount had no Tableau value and then correctly pushed back on the first answer ('Profit, Sales and Quantity are also raw columns, how come those are shown?'). ROOT CAUSE: parity.TABLEAU_TRUTH is a hand-typed module-level dict holding ONE datasource ('Sample - Superstore') and THREE columns (SALES/PROFIT/QUANTITY) from the era when Superstore was the only demo workbook; check_workbook() reads it and nothing else for the raw-column table. So Discount showed '-' on the very workbook that dict covers, and EVERY raw measure on EVERY other workbook would show '-' permanently regardless of how live the REST connection was. R1/R2's dynamic pull_live_tableau_truth already existed but was only ever handed res['calc_metrics'] -- raw columns, the EASIEST thing to match (a view exporting SUM(Discount) maps straight onto the Discount measure), were never offered to the matcher at all. FIX: new parity.raw_measure_metrics(result) adapts raw-column rows into the SAME {name, metric, sql} shape truth_from_view_csv already matches (ONE matcher for both kinds, deliberately -- two matchers drifting is this project's most-repeated bug class); _raw_truth_key() namespaces them so they can never collide with a cortex_semantic metric name; apply_live_truth_to_measures() folds REST values back into the measure rows and re-judges; _resummarize() re-rolls the roll-up (without it Stage 5 would print '13/13 pass' above a BUG row). pipeline_app.py Stage 5 RESTRUCTURED so the pull runs ABOVE the tables (it previously ran after the raw-column table had already rendered) and is handed calc metrics + raw measures together, so real Tableau values now reach the raw-column table, the calc table AND the downloadable notebook; the per-view REST notes expander moved out of the calc_metrics block so a workbook with zero calculated fields still shows them. VERDICT RULE, deliberate: an EXACT reference (single-row Tableau view) that disagrees flips the verdict to BUG exactly like the hand-verified figure it replaces; an APPROXIMATE one (multi-row view, column-summed) NEVER decides a verdict -- a view can carry its own filter, so treating that as a BUG would manufacture the same false-BUG class this project has already been bitten by twice -- it is recorded, labelled '(REST, ~ sum of N rows)' in every surface, and left for a human/Cortex to weigh. Gate test_raw_measure_live_truth_and_json_verdicts (raw-measure adaptation, EXACT-vs-APPROXIMATE verdict rules, summary re-roll, no-match no-op). Teeth proven by reverting the fix (raw measures not offered to the matcher; approximate allowed to flip a verdict) -- both revert to a failing gate. Reproduced the user's exact screenshot state first (13/13 pass, Discount tableau=None) to confirm the diagnosis before changing anything, and re-confirmed the manual-upload path (no REST connection) is byte-identical, with the hardcoded dict remaining the honest fallback there. Suite 69 -> 70 auto-run gates, all green; validate_numbers exact; pyflakes clean. FIRST LIVE RUN WORKED MECHANICALLY BUT EXPOSED A REAL FLAW IN THE APPROXIMATE TIER (2026-07-30, same day): Quantity came back as '231924.0 (REST, ~ sum of 24 rows)' -- a value no previous code path could have produced, so the wiring is confirmed live -- but the number is WRONG, exactly 6x the app's true 38,654, because the 24-row view's rows did not PARTITION the data (the same quantity appeared six times over). The verdict guard held (an approximate reference never decides, so nothing was falsely failed) but an authoritative-looking 231,924 next to the true 38,654 is worse than showing nothing. This is the disclosed risk of the 2026-07-29 user-directed sum-across-rows trade-off materializing immediately: the assumption behind it ('multi-row means a clean dimension breakdown') is false for real Tableau views. FIXED with parity._rows_partition_data(headers, rows) -- summing across rows is valid ONLY if each row is a distinct slice, checked from the CSV ALONE via two signals: (1) a Measure Names/Measure Values column (Tableau's own marker for a measure crosstab, where every dimension row repeats once per measure) and (2) duplicate dimension tuples (if the non-numeric columns don't uniquely identify each row, the rows repeat by construction; a multi-row view with no dimension column at all can't be a clean breakdown either). Deliberately NOT validated against the app's own value -- an 'independent' reference checked by the very thing it exists to check is not independent. A failing view is skipped with a STATED reason instead of summed. Proven not to over-refuse: a genuine partitioned breakdown still approximates and the single-row EXACT path is untouched. ALSO: the per-view REST notes now carry each view's ACTUAL exported column headers (surfaced in the UI as 'Columns Tableau exported'), which is the direct answer to 'why does measure X have no Tableau value?' -- if no view exports a Discount column then Tableau never renders Discount in that workbook and '-' is the honest result, not a matching failure; previously that question could only be answered by guessing. Gate extended (repeated-row/crosstab/no-dimension shapes each refused with a reason, genuine breakdown still approximated, notes carry real columns); teeth proven by disabling the partition guard. Suite unchanged at 70 auto-run gates, all green. Still awaiting a live re-run. OPTION 1 BUILT 2026-08-04 (user's explicit choice after the 6x-Quantity finding, over dropping the tier or relabeling it 'corroboration'): the unsound sum-across-rows tier is REMOVED, not patched a third time -- summing a rendered view's column is correct only when its rows partition the data, which is NOT reliably decidable from a CSV alone (a crosstab inflates, a filter deflates, a legitimate detail listing has repeated dimensions while still being summable and is indistinguishable from a crosstab by shape alone). TRUE Tableau aggregates now come from the VizQL Data Service instead: new tableau_server.list_datasources()/vds_query_aggregate() ask Tableau's OWN ENGINE for SUM(field) with NO grouping fields, which returns exactly one row -- the real grand total, needing no dashboard to display a total and immune to both inflation and deflation since no view is queried at all. HONEST FAILURE MODE STATED, not hidden: a workbook published with EMBEDDED data (bundles its own extract) has no separately-published datasource for VDS to query at all; pull_tableau_aggregates detects zero datasources and returns a stated reason rather than a silent empty result. Wired into parity.pull_vds_tableau_truth() (restricted to pure-SUM metrics) and Stage 5 (VDS queried first as authoritative, the single-row-exact view-CSV path as fallback, a new 'Tableau's own aggregates (VizQL Data Service)' panel showing which datasource answered what). Gates: test_r2_live_truth_pull rewritten (multi-row now asserts NOTHING is contributed) and test_raw_measure_live_truth_and_json_verdicts extended with the full VDS orchestration. Teeth proven on three fronts. Suite unchanged at 70 gates, all green; validate_numbers exact; pyflakes clean. No new dependency. STILL OPEN: not yet live-verified -- if the test workbook has no separately-published datasource, VDS will correctly report that reason and Discount will still show '-', now the truthful answer rather than a matcher bug. SAME SILENT-NON-RENDER BUG SHIPPED A SECOND TIME 2026-08-04, DIFFERENT SECTION: after the VDS build (above), user reported 'Discount still not showing' with a screenshot showing NEITHER the REST expander NOR the new VDS panel anywhere, and the old hardcoded Sales/Profit/Quantity values with no (REST) tag -- proving none of this session's code ran at all. Root cause: the whole raw-column Tableau-value section is 'if _conn: ...' with NO else, so a FILE-UPLOADED workbook ('_conn' only set via the Pull-from-Tableau-Server flow) renders NOTHING here -- the exact same bug class as the earlier 'visual validation not working' incident, shipped a second time because the first fix targeted only the section that broke, not every section sharing the same gate variable. Fixed with an elif stating plainly that dynamic values need the Tableau REST fetch flow, not a file upload. Also fixed a stale caption still describing the REMOVED approximate-sum behavior. THE STANDING FIX: AST-scanned the whole file for every top-level _conn-gated UI block; found a third candidate that turned out to be a correctly-excluded nested detail check inside an already-informative branch. New PERMANENT gate test_no_silent_conn_gated_ui statically asserts every top-level _conn-gated Streamlit UI block carries an else/elif -- converts 'state the reason' from a rule violated twice into something the suite enforces for any future _conn-gated section. Teeth proven by reverting the fix and confirming the gate fails with the exact line number. Verified by direct count (not assumed): 67 ok + 4 skip = 71 auto-run gates. REAL BUG FOUND ON THE FIRST LIVE VDS CLICK 2026-08-04: user's screenshot showed the REST-view panel now working correctly (every view honestly reported as a multi-row dimension breakdown, never summed) -- but the NEW VizQL Data Service panel showed EVERY published datasource on the site (10+, including 'Sample - Superstore') failing identically: TableauAuthError HTTP 400 'No acceptable representation'. This proved the site genuinely HAS published datasources (not the embedded-data case) and auth/sign-in succeeded (it got far enough to be refused per-datasource, not per-session) -- a real, fixable bug, not a structural limit. ROOT CAUSE: TableauRestClient._headers() hardcoded Accept to 'application/xml' regardless of the requested content_type -- so the VDS calls (content_type='application/json', a JSON-ONLY API with no XML representation at all) sent Content-Type: application/json but Accept: application/xml, a textbook HTTP content-negotiation mismatch that Tableau correctly rejected on every single call. This bug was INVISIBLE to the gate written for the VDS build, which asserted the request BODY shape but never checked the headers -- exactly where the bug lived. FIXED: _headers() now defaults Accept to match content_type unless explicitly overridden, so both VDS calls (which already passed content_type='application/json') are automatically corrected; the classic XML REST API (every other caller) is completely unaffected, since its default content_type is still 'application/xml'. GATED: extended the VDS section of test_raw_measure_live_truth_and_json_verdicts to capture and assert the ACTUAL headers sent (Accept and Content-Type both application/json for VDS), plus a direct assertion that a bare _headers() call for the classic API is unchanged. Teeth proven by reverting to the EXACT broken header logic that shipped to the real account and confirming the gate fails with the precise diagnosis. Suite unchanged in count (extended, not duplicated), all green; pyflakes clean. Not yet re-verified live -- awaiting redeploy + a re-click to confirm Discount and every other measure now resolve from a real Tableau aggregate. 2026-08-07 SUPERSEDED (explicit user decision, not merely extended). See R12's own 2026-08-07 note for what the pack itself gained (real Tableau evidence + the three bugs found fixing it). Deployed live.

roadmap.detail: DONE 2026-07-26. Both halves now shipped. (1) REUSE half (2026-07-25): pipeline.resolve_existing_table finds an existing table ANYWHERE in the DB (LOAD_SCHEMA first, else any schema e.g. WBR_DB.PUBLIC from the corpus load) and repoints config at its real location - fixed the E-Commerce 'Customers (DataDNA...)' extract that exists in PUBLIC but not PIPELINE_DEMO. Both onboarding paths wired (pipeline.onboard + init_workbook --connection, sharing one resolver per the standing sync rule); Stage 1 shows both what bound and what was refused. Gate test_auto_bind_existing_snowflake_table (11 cases incl. the wrong-table guard, ambiguity, corpus XML shapes, no-copy assertion). TWO REAL GOTCHAS FOUND GETTING THERE, worth keeping documented so nobody re-discovers them the hard way: (1) a Snowflake stage's DEFAULT encryption (client-side) is NOT supported as an AI_COMPLETE file input source -- 'Input files from stages with Client Side Encryption is not supported.' The stage must be created (or recreated) with `ENCRYPTION = (TYPE = 'SNOWFLAKE_SSE')` explicitly; the default `CREATE STAGE` will NOT work for this. (2) PROMPT() requires an explicit `{0}` placeholder in the prompt text marking where the file argument binds in -- omitting it does not error, it silently returns NULL, which look like a broken vision call when it is actually a syntax issue. CONFIRMED WORKING CALL SHAPE (for reuse when building the actual R8 diff): `AI_COMPLETE('claude-opus-5', PROMPT('Describe what you see in this image: {0}', TO_FILE('@stage_with_SSE_encryption', 'file.png')))`. GATED: new test_vision_validate_dashboard -- ensure_vision_stage's SQL text asserted to request SNOWFLAKE_SSE explicitly, _describe_image_via_cortex's SQL text asserted to carry the {0} placeholder (the exact thing that silently returns NULL if omitted, found live), a null-response and a raising-session case both proven to become stated errors, _compare_descriptions_via_cortex asserted to be genuinely plain-text (no TO_FILE/PROMPT in its SQL -- proving it never attempts the untested multi-image shape), the full orchestration proven against a fake multi-call session (both images actually staged with their real bytes verified, correct verdict/explanation/tokens on success, UNKNOWN + recorded errors + comparison-call-skipped on a failed description). Suite 67->68. Pyflakes clean. WIRED INTO pipeline_app.py Stage 5: a new 'Visual validation (Cortex vision)' section, shown only when the workbook came from the Tableau REST fetch flow (_conn, now scoped above the calc_metrics block so R8 can use it independent of whether the workbook has any calculated-field metrics) AND a live Snowflake session exists. FIRST LIVE TEST FOUND TWO REAL BUGS, BOTH FIXED SAME SESSION 2026-07-29: user deployed and clicked 'Run visual validation'. BUG 1 -- FALSE 'BUG' FLOOD: 8/8 calc metrics showed Cortex verdict BUG with explanations like 'Tableau's value is unknown/missing.' Root cause: cortex_judge_section (R2 path, same live run) was being called with tv_lit='unknown' (a literal string) whenever a metric had NEITHER a live_truth entry NOR a tableau_bound -- Cortex correctly cannot validate a real number against the word 'unknown' and reasonably answered BUG, but displaying that as a bug misrepresented 'nothing to compare against' as a real defect. FIX: both pipeline_app.py's live judge loop AND parity.build_section_validation_notebook now detect this case (tv_lit is None) and skip Cortex ENTIRELY, showing 'NO REFERENCE' instead -- matching check_calc_metrics' own EXECUTED semantics (ran clean, no independent truth, never a bug on its own). New parity._no_reference_cell() for the notebook path; _bug_summary_cell() updated to track no_reference separately from real bugs/unknowns/disagreements. GATED: test_section_validation_notebook extended with a third fixture metric carrying tableau_bound=None -- asserts it generates ZERO Cortex calls (exactly 2, not 3) and is reported as NO_REFERENCE, locking this exact bug down. BUG 2 -- STREAMLIT CRASH: clicking 'Run visual validation' crashed with `StreamlitDuplicateElementKey: There are multiple elements with the same key='Order Details::Order Date::None'` inside engine.build_where's st.date_input call. ROOT CAUSE: the live app already renders each dashboard once (its own preview pass), registering INPUT WIDGETS (date pickers, filter dropdowns, Drill selectboxes, worksheet-shown parameters) keyed by dashboard/sheet/field name; the R8 headless path then called the REAL engine.build_where()/engine.render_sheet() a SECOND time for the SAME dashboard to compute where_parts and render sheets, re-creating the IDENTICAL keys -- Streamlit enforces global key uniqueness per script run, so this always collided, not an occasional flake. FIX (headless_render.py): new _mocked_widgets() context manager -- monkeypatches EVERY Streamlit input-widget function (selectbox/date_input/number_input/text_input/multiselect/checkbox/slider) to return a sensible non-interactive default (selectbox -> first option = this project's own 'All' convention; date_input -> its given full-range value unchanged; etc.) instead of registering a real widget, for the duration of a headless render -- same technique already used for altair_chart/plotly_chart capture, now covering every widget-creating function, not just charts. render_sheet_to_png wraps its engine.render_sheet() call in this context (a SHEET can carry its own Drill dropdown/parameter, not just the dashboard-level filter row); render_dashboard_to_png computes its OWN where_parts default the same way when the caller doesn't supply one. pipeline_app.py's R8 wiring simplified to stop calling the widget-creating engine.build_where(dash) itself -- now just calls HR.render_dashboard_to_png(dash) and lets it handle this safely. VERIFIED by direct call-counting against the REAL Superstore fixture (not just 'output looks right'): simulated the live preview's real build_where() call first (1 real selectbox call, reproducing the actual collision setup), then confirmed the headless path makes ZERO real selectbox/date_input calls and still produces the identical correct PNG (276,931 bytes, unchanged). GATED: new test_headless_render_never_touches_real_widgets -- counts actual calls to the real widget functions during a headless render (must be 0 in every case), proves render_sheet_to_png alone has the same guarantee (not just the dashboard-level composite), proves restoration afterward. Suite 68->69. Pyflakes clean on headless_render.py/pipeline_app.py. Redeployed pipeline_demo with both fixes. A THIRD REAL BUG FOUND ON THE RE-TEST 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION: after redeploying the two fixes above, the user's real workbook showed ALL 10 dashboards SKIPPED -- 8 as 'no matching Tableau view image found', 2 as 'app rendered no chart'. Diagnosed from the actual view list the user shared: Tableau REST returns each view's INTERNAL name (e.g. 'Commission Model', 'Customers', 'Overview'), NOT the dashboard's customizable display TITLE (e.g. 'Sales Commission Model', 'Customer Analysis', 'Executive Overview - Profitability') -- the matching code only ever checked the title. FIX: the IR already carries both dash['name'] (the raw internal Tableau name -- what REST actually returns) and dash['title'] (the display caption) from tableau_parser.dashboards(); matching now tries dash['name'] FIRST, dash['title'] as a fallback for workbooks where they happen to be identical. The other 2 skips ('app rendered no chart') are EXPECTED, not a bug -- Order Details (35,777 rows) and Sheet 22 are table/detail views, and headless_render's documented scope is Altair-rendered CHARTS only; a raw data-table sheet has nothing to capture as a chart image, correctly reported rather than faked. STILL OPEN, HONESTLY: the view-name fix has NOT been re-clicked in Snowsight yet this pass (pyflakes + full suite clean, but no new gate added since this is a one-line lookup-order change inside existing, already-gated matching logic) -- ask the user to redeploy and re-run to confirm dashboards now match. Also still open from the original scope: real AI-token metering feeding the Run Center's panels beyond the sidebar total (a presentation-layer follow-up, not a capability gap); vl-convert-python's Snowflake-conda-channel availability is still unconfirmed; table/detail-sheet PNG export (Order Details, Sheet 22 class) remains out of scope, Altair charts only; and the pre-existing 'entire page reruns/blanks' UX issue (Streamlit reruns the whole ~600-line run_pipeline() on every widget interaction, no caching) remains a separate, real, deliberately-deferred follow-up. TWO MORE REAL BUGS FOUND + FIXED 2026-07-30, from the user's live results table (7 dashboards reading 'UNKNOWN', raw escaped JSON dumped in the Note column). BUG A -- EVERY VISION VERDICT WAS UNKNOWN BECAUSE THE JSON WAS NEVER PARSED: the note text was `"{\"verdict\": \"BUG\", ...}"`, i.e. a JSON *string* CONTAINING the JSON object. AI_COMPLETE returns a VARIANT, and stringifying a VARIANT yields its JSON REPRESENTATION (quoted + backslash-escaped), not its bare text -- so _extract_json_obj hit the `\"` escape immediately after the opening brace and failed on every candidate `{`. Cortex's verdicts were perfectly well-formed and simply never being read; the UI was reporting a parser failure as an inconclusive result. FIX: _extract_json_obj now peels up to a few layers of JSON-string encoding (bounded, never a while-True) before the existing brace scan. Affects BOTH R8's vision comparison and R2's cortex_judge_section, which share the parser. BUG B -- THE DIFF WAS COMPARING A FULL DASHBOARD AGAINST A DELIBERATELY PARTIAL RENDER, PRODUCING FALSE BUGs: with the verdicts finally readable they said things like 'the migrated app is missing the KPI summary panel' and 'omits five of the six region-level KPIs'. Those are NOT migration defects -- headless_render draws Altair CHARTS only, so KPI tiles and Plotly/map sheets are absent from the app-side PNG BY DESIGN (the live app renders them correctly; only the static exporter cannot), and Cortex was never told. FIX: parity._omitted_sheets() reads the non-rendered sheet names out of headless_render's own per-sheet notes; _compare_descriptions_via_cortex gained an app_render_notes arg that injects a CRITICAL CONTEXT caveat naming those sheets and stating their absence is expected and must not be reported as a bug (if the only differences found are these known-absent sheets, the verdict is PASS); vision_validate_dashboard threads the notes through and returns omitted_sheets, which pipeline_app.py appends to every result row ('not compared (chart-only exporter cannot draw these): ...') so a verdict over a partial image can never read as a verdict over the whole dashboard. Gates: test_vision_validate_dashboard EXTENDED (caveat present and names each omitted sheet, a sheet that DID render is never listed as omitted, the call stays plain-text, no-notes injects no caveat) plus the double-encoded JSON shape locked in test_raw_measure_live_truth_and_json_verdicts alongside every previously-working shape and the garbage-stays-None case. Teeth proven by reverting both fixes (pre-fix JSON parser; caveat removed) -- each reverts to a failing gate. Suite 69 -> 70 auto-run gates, all green; pyflakes clean. HARDENED + MADE PERSISTENT 2026-07-30 (second pass, after the user reported 'visual doesnt work' with no visible error): each dashboard's app-side render and vision call are now individually wrapped, so one failure reports its real error text in its OWN row instead of aborting the whole run and losing every dashboard that did work (same resilience rule the REST pulls already follow); an app-side render returning None now names WHICH sheets failed and why, instead of one generic message. CRITICALLY, the results are now stashed in session_state and rendered OUTSIDE the `if st.button(...)` block -- previously they existed only inside it, so the next widget interaction anywhere on the page silently WIPED them (this app re-runs the whole ~600-line run_pipeline on every interaction -- the known, separately-tracked caching issue), which is exactly what 'it doesn't work' looks like from the outside even when every underlying call succeeded. A 'Clear visual validation results' button keeps the stash recoverable. DEPENDENCY RISK CLOSED THE SAME PASS: vl-convert-python -- flagged since 2026-07-28 as the highest-risk dependency in environment.yml (a compiled Rust binary wheel, materially less likely for a curated conda channel to carry than the pure-Python additions) -- is CONFIRMED PRESENT on the snowflake channel at 1.9.0.post1, queried live via INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PACKAGES, alongside requests 2.34.2, pillow 9.4.0, fpdf2 2.8.7, openpyxl 3.1.5, altair 6.0.0 and plotly 6.7.0. environment.yml's comments updated from 'NOT YET CONFIRMED' to the real measured versions, so R8's PNG pipeline has no remaining dependency blocker. Still awaiting a live re-run to confirm the verdicts now read PASS/BUG instead of UNKNOWN and that the KPI-panel false BUGs are gone. 'VISUAL VALIDATION NOT WORKING' ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-30 (third pass, after the user reported it twice with no visible error): the cause was a SILENT NON-RENDER, not a failure. Diagnosed by running the real code path rather than asking again -- vl_convert imports and render_dashboard_to_png produces real PNGs locally (276,931 B / 133,916 B / 64,262 B for three real dashboards); INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PACKAGES confirms vl-convert-python 1.9.0.post1 is available; and the FULL Cortex vision half works end to end against the real account through our own functions (ensure_vision_stage -> _stage_png -> _describe_image_via_cortex returned a genuinely accurate 1,159-token description of a real rendered dashboard). Every piece worked. The section's guard is `if _conn and in_sf and ir.get('dashboards'):` with NO else -- so when any precondition is missing the ENTIRE section (heading, button, everything) renders NOTHING. _conn is set ONLY for a workbook fetched via 'Pull from Tableau Server/Cloud' and is deliberately cleared for a FILE UPLOAD (an uploaded file has no live Tableau view, so the Tableau half of the comparison genuinely cannot exist) -- so a file-uploaded workbook shows no visual-validation UI at all, indistinguishable from the feature being broken. FIXED with an elif branch that always renders the heading and states exactly which precondition is missing and how to satisfy it (load via Connect -> project -> workbook -> Fetch; or note that CORTEX AI_COMPLETE doesn't exist against local DuckDB) -- this project's own 'an unavailable capability states its reason' rule, which this section quietly violated. roadmap.item: R12 — Proof-first per-CHART validation pack (adopted + hardened a user-supplied reference implementation)
roadmap.detail: DONE 2026-08-05. User supplied accelerator_validation_reference/ (dependency-free Python: validation_report.py comparison engine + renderer, README requiring the accelerator to supply Tableau/Streamlit/backend adapters). Vendored it as validation_report.py and wrote validation_adapter.py (the adapters), wired into Stage 5 as a downloadable ZIP pack (HTML + validation_summary.json + issues.csv + one comparison.csv per chart); both added to snowflake.yml artifacts (bundle gate now counts 20 modules). REAL UPGRADE over the existing section-level tables: compares EVERY ROW at each chart's own displayed grain (three-way Tableau/Streamlit/backend), not grand totals — a total can reconcile while individual marks are wrong in compensating directions. Tolerance is PRECISION-DERIVED from the workbook's own number format (IR's fmt: cur0 -> +/-$0.50) instead of a flat relative percentage. KEY DESIGN: the Streamlit leg is the app's OWN captured chart dataframe (headless_render.capture_sheet_chart -> chart.data), never a second run of the backend SQL (would be circular); the column mapping (engine.py's internal aliases VAL/DIM/T/FLAG/PANEL/... are NOT Tableau captions) is READ from the rendered chart's own Vega-Lite encoding + the sheet spec's caption for that channel, never guessed — unresolvable leaves the chart NOT_VALIDATED; the backend query is SCOPED to the chart's displayed keys, which fixed two real false-failure bugs found live (a top-N chart comparing 30 displayed vs 800 unscoped backend rows; a monthly chart comparing 48 monthly vs 1242 daily rows from a missing DATE_TRUNC). FOUR genuine bugs fixed IN the user-supplied reference (its own 9 tests still pass; the reference folder was restored byte-identical to as-supplied, patches applied only to this project's vendored copy): (1) list(None) crash made its own advertised BLOCKED path unreachable; (2) a wholly-absent source reported FAIL ('proven wrong') instead of BLOCKED ('never measured'); (3) all-or-nothing cell comparison hid the provable Streamlit-vs-backend agreement whenever Tableau was absent (the common case for a file-uploaded workbook) — now each available PAIR is judged on its merits while the chart still cannot PASS without Tableau proof; (4) added skip_reason support so an unextractable chart is BLOCKED WITH ITS REASON rather than silently omitted (an omitted chart is indistinguishable from a validated one). TWO more false-failure classes found and fixed in this project's OWN adapter during live iteration: a numpy.bool_ grain value fell through to str() as the literal text 'True', matching nothing in a real boolean column, and a scoped-backend-returns-zero-rows case (an adapter limitation) was initially reported as every displayed value FAILED — both now refuse with a stated reason instead of shipping a false failure. KPI/text-only sheets (a dashboard's most-read numbers, e.g. the Executive Overview headline row) were originally excluded entirely (no Altair chart to capture) — added headless_render.capture_sheet_kpis (captures the REAL st.metric/columns().metric calls) + validation_adapter.build_kpi_chart_spec, validating each KPI tile as its own measure with its own number-format tolerance, comparing the DISPLAYED (rounded) value against a full-precision backend aggregate (e.g. displayed $2,326,534 vs backend $2,326,534.354, diff $0.354, within +/-$0.50 -> PASS). An aggregate/window-grain calculated dimension (a FIXED LOD or table calc used as a colour series) is precomputed in a base CTE and filtered on the alias — the SAME pattern engine.py itself uses for these calcs — rather than refused outright. Coverage on Superstore: 5/20 charts comparable (up from an initial 3/20), workbook decision honestly BLOCKED (no Tableau REST export for this file-uploaded run = no key-set authority), 0 failed values across every comparable chart. Gate test_validation_pack_adapter. REMAINING, biggest lever: engine.py does not set real Tableau captions as chart axis/tooltip titles (same root cause as R11's tooltip gap) — fixing that would unblock most of the remaining 'unnamed channel' (VAL/ROWLAB/X0) blocks. Deliberately not done this session: it changes the shipped app's visuals, so it needs its own decision, not a validation-tooling side effect. 2026-08-07 UPDATE — wired the user-supplied validation_evidence_bridge.py in, closing exactly the "REMAINING, biggest lever" gap named above for the chart kinds it can reach. _build_validation_pack now calls VEB.build_complete_validation_spec instead of validation_adapter directly: real Tableau REST dashboard screenshots (tableau_server.pull_all_view_images) paired with real Streamlit-rendered screenshots (kept in SEPARATE files, never the same image compared against itself) with a computed structural similarity score; real per-worksheet Tableau crosstab rows (pull_all_view_csvs) or an uploaded-CSV fallback matched by canonical filename; and engine.EVIDENCE_CAPTURE (default False, zero-cost off) turns on only for the pack build so r_map/r_treemap/r_table/the rank-table branch of r_circle — kinds the Vega-Lite-encoding guess can never see at all, since they render via Plotly/st.dataframe/hand-built HTML — record their OWN real final dataframe via VEB.REGISTRY.record_chart. Detail/list tables cap recorded evidence at the top 30 displayed rows (2026-08-07 user decision), not the full up-to-200 displayed set. THREE real bugs found live and fixed same session: (1) a duplicate registry entry under an empty dashboard name, from capture_sheet_kpis' own second render pass over a sheet the Altair capture already tried — fixed by threading dashboard_name through it too, plus making the recorder idempotent per (dashboard, sheet); (2) Tableau REST's view list is DASHBOARD-granular, not per-worksheet (confirmed live: 9 dashboards, 9 views) — fixed with a same-dashboard-name fallback, restricted to the unambiguous 1-sheet-per-dashboard case only; (3) headless_render.capture_sheet_chart's st.altair_chart monkeypatch OVERWROTE on every call instead of collecting them, so a multi-panel sheet (r_mbar's one small-multiple per measure, faceted small-multiples) lost every panel but the last in its screenshot — found from a user image comparison (Superstore's CustomerOverview showed 1 of 6 KPI panels), fixed by capturing every call and combining with alt.hconcat. Live-verified against the real account (site b360bi, workbook 'R1 Test Upload - Superstore'): real screenshots for 9/9 dashboards (similarity 0.72-0.85, one at 0.852 scored PASS), real backend numbers matching the app's own displayed numbers exactly where both resolve (Sales by Geography: 49/49 rows exact). Still open, not regressions: Tableau's crosstab sometimes returns a long/pivoted shape (Measure Names/Measure Values) the aligner correctly refuses to reshape; date-part-grouped Tableau headers (Month of Order Date) don't yet alias to a chart's own Order Date grain; two measures (Days to Ship Scheduled, Sales Forecast) don't resolve against the backend table. All 75 regression gates green. Deployed live to WBR_DB.PUBLIC.TABLEAU_TO_SIS_PIPELINE_DEMO. 2026-08-07 LATER — client-facing report added: validation_report_dashboard.py, built to the user's supplied sample structure. A SECOND renderer over the SAME already-validated run dict (decides nothing; the vendored engine and its test_validation_pack_adapter lock are untouched): per-dashboard chapters with a stat strip, A visual comparison (both images + structural score + Cortex verdict), B chart index + chart DATA CONTRACT (grain, measures, T/S/B shapes, key/order check, max diff) + expandable per-chart records with PAIRWISE verdicts (Tableau<->Streamlit, Streamlit<->Backend, Tableau<->Backend), C logic/calculation, D filters/interactions, then consolidated exceptions, evidence & reproducibility and a sign-off record. Deliberate deviation: the sample's '98.1% pixel similarity' and 'max shift 4px' are NOT reproduced — we cannot honestly measure them (the app image is a headless re-render, not a screenshot of the SSO-gated deployed app, so there is no pixel registration); the real structural score is shown, labelled triage-only. A REAL APP BUG was caught this pass: Product Detail Sheet's Discount went BLOCKED -> FAIL, and checking TABLEAU ITSELF via REST settled it — Tableau 0.2/0.8/0.4, app 0.1/0.2/0.1, backend 0.2/0.8/0.4. The validation was right and the migrated app is wrong: profile_superstore.py curates 'Discount': AVG(DISCOUNT), and because Discount is a RAW COLUMN that curated AVG silently beats the workbook's own declared agg=sum. NOT FIXED — the fix changes numbers the DEPLOYED app renders and AVG is legitimately correct on other sheets, so it needs an explicit decision. snowflake.yml 23 -> 24 artifacts. NOT DEPLOYED. 2026-08-10/12 UPDATE -- the image evidence source was REPLACED, not patched: app_screenshot.py launches the GENERATED app locally (streamlit run, real Chromium via Playwright) and screenshots every dashboard tab for real, after the user asked directly — mid-way through a third round of headless-render bugfixes — "why are you rendering it again, just screenshot the app." The old headless re-render (a SECOND renderer) had been quietly FLATTERING the migration: on Customer Analysis it drew all 30 customer names because it gave the chart more height than the app does, while the real app correctly drops every other label. headless_render.render_dashboard_to_png is no longer called for the pack's IMAGE leg (still supplies the Streamlit DATA leg via capture_sheet_chart, untouched); when no browser is available (inside the deployed SiS app itself, which has none), visual evidence is BLOCKED with that stated reason, never a fallback render -- real, accepted cost: packs must be generated from a workstation, matching how they already are (the Tableau REST connection lives there too). Found and fixed getting this working: a subprocess stdout=PIPE left undrained deadlocked the child Streamlit process after ~2 dashboards (every later tab timed out and looked like a slow/broken app for two full investigation rounds; fixed by redirecting to a file -- capture time 646s -> 137s in the same move). STATUS-ROLLUP BUG fixed same arc: a dashboard's status was the WORST of visual+chart+formula+interaction statuses, so ONE missing screenshot alone read the whole dashboard BLOCKED even when every chart/formula/interaction had genuinely passed -- meaning the accelerator could never show PASS on anything if run from inside its own deployed Streamlit-in-Snowflake app (no browser there). Fixed: a BLOCKED visual (missing evidence) is excluded from the rollup; a visual that WAS captured and found genuinely wrong (FAIL/REVIEW) still counts exactly as before -- 'no proof, no pass' still holds for the visual claim itself. PACK SLIMMED (2026-08-08 user ask, 'keep only what is necessary'): 49 files/5.7MB -> ~11 files, ships as INDIVIDUAL downloadable files (no zip -- explicit user decision, a zip put a download-unpack-hunt step between a reviewer and the one file they wanted), screenshots inlined as base64 so each HTML report is fully self-contained, a generated README.md carries the status legend + the filter-state caveat (app renders at 'All', Tableau carries its saved state, so a filtered dashboard's visual difference can be state, not defect) + a manifest built from what is ACTUALLY on disk. 2026-08-11/12 -- tried against a SECOND corpus workbook (Regional Analysis, at the user's request) and a live Tableau connection for the first time this pack has been run against one for real, which surfaced FOUR more real bugs, all fixed and gate-locked: (1) every stacked-bar/line-with-labels chart reported 'captured chart exposed no dataframe to compare' -- engine.py's bar+text pattern is an Altair LayerChart whose top-level .data stays Undefined unless every layer shares the exact dataframe, which the text-label layer's derived columns (a stacking cumulative offset) always breaks; the real rows were one attribute away on chart.layer[0].data. Fixed by walking every layer/hconcat/vconcat/concat and preferring the first candidate with the FULL needed column set. (2) The pie chart's theta channel had no Vega-Lite title (color did), so it was the one channel with no resolvable Tableau caption; engine.r_pie now titles theta from the measure caption too. (3) Tableau's dashboard-level crosstab export for a MULTI-SHEET dashboard returns ONE sheet's data, not per-worksheet, and the existing matcher discarded it outright for any multi-sheet dashboard ('that would be guessing'). Fixed with a CONTENT match, not a guess: a sheet's own declared fields (parity._sheet_pill_captions) must EXACTLY equal the crosstab's header columns (a looser subset match was tried first and found genuinely ambiguous live -- View2's real 3-column header subset-matched BOTH 'Region level Sales' and 'Profit by Category'); the exact match resolves uniquely, refuses when more than one sheet qualifies. (4) Tableau's own crosstab formats numbers with a thousands comma ('163,797.1638'), which Decimal() rejected outright -- every Tableau-side value silently parsed to None, never reported wrong, just never actually compared (a chart could read PASS on streamlit-vs-backend agreement alone while the Tableau leg was never checked at all). validation_report._d() now strips the comma first, matching the same handling already applied to Tableau-sourced numbers elsewhere in this project. Live-verified end to end against Regional Analysis Dashboard on the real account (prod-useast-b.online.tableau.com, site b360bi): real Tableau screenshots + real crosstabs pulled for both dashboards, genuine structural scores computed (View1 0.844 REVIEW, View2 0.880 PASS, not BLOCKED-for-no-evidence), every chart now produces real Tableau+Streamlit+backend rows, and every compared VALUE reconciles within tolerance on both fully-evidenced charts. One real, separate, DELIBERATELY NOT silently patched finding surfaced by this: both those charts still read chart-level FAIL solely from order_match (an exact ROW-SEQUENCE check) despite every cell passing -- meaningful for a ranked list, not for a grouped bar chart where display order carries no visual meaning; flagged to the user rather than loosening the vendored engine's strictness unilaterally. A third corpus workbook (Global Sales Dashboard) was opened during this session's screenshot testing and its View2 dashboard crashed the re-render-based capture -- surfaced, then superseded before being diagnosed: the conversation moved to the real-screenshot rewrite before this crash was root-caused.
